name: Anhedral Voss
aliases: the face-reader of the Exhausted Seam

identity.realm: Qi path, seven ordinary vessels open and the eighth closing. The eighth is the liver, and the eighth is where the grit goes, so the gate he is working toward is the organ he is wearing out doing the work that qualifies him to work toward it.

appearance.presentation: A short, thick-necked man whose breath is audible before his words are, because it carries. He is written into an instrument rather than a person: the guild, the crews on the heap and his own physician all read his chest before they read anything else on him.
appearance.age: Late for an ashwalker and early for nothing else. The grit in his blood shortens the ordinary span, so he has roughly the years of a commonborn and the intake of something older and worse.
appearance.build: Barrel-chested and low, with a permanently half-lunged right side where the loading caught him, and forearms developed out of carrying spoil sacks rather than out of any discipline.
appearance.complexion: Grey-pitted, with a fine grey dust worked into every crease and into the corners of the eyes, so that in low light he reads as the same colour as the ground he certifies.
appearance.hair: Cropped short and stiff with grit, and it never lies flat again after a shift. He keeps it cropped because anything longer carries a measurable load of what he breathed.
appearance.eyes: Watery and reddened at the rims, quick to close when the air is bad, which is the reflex of a man deciding whether he can afford the next hour.
appearance.palette: Ash grey, wet stone black, and one bleached ochre on the guild seal and the shift collar. The value range is compressed on purpose: he is a shape that sits inside a drift.
appearance.attire: A canvas shift with the guild seal stitched at the shoulder, sleeves cut off above the elbow so his forearms can be read at a glance, and a leather mouth-cloth he takes off more out of courtesy than out of need.
appearance.marks: Grey grit shadowing both forearms to the elbow, deepest at the wrists where he sets the sack down, and an old split at the left hairline from a face that came down without warning.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried, and turned slightly side-on at all times, so the nearer shoulder always faces the drift and his chest is never quite square to whoever he is speaking to.

canon.role_in_story: The Exhausted Seam's only face-reader: the officer who certifies that a working face is still workable on the strength of standing in it. He is right more often than not, because no softer body survives the reading, and he is the only man who can afford to keep standing there. He has never certified his own, and the guild has never asked, because a certificate is evidence and a man breathing is not.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the lip of the Exhausted Seam holding a lantern down and a lantern-mirror up at the same time, counting his own breaths aloud against a tally board while a drift loaded behind him and did not move, which is how the guild learned the seam had stopped breathing two seasons before anyone filed a report.
canon.lore: An ashwalker takes volcanic grit into the lung and keeps it, so the intake that would destroy softer tissue is a working condition rather than an injury. The mineral load settles in the blood, and the first place it settles is the liver, and the liver is the last of the twelve ordinary vessels and opens at the eighth rung. That single ordering is Voss's whole life: the intake that keeps him alive is the intake carrying him toward a gate, and the gate does not open because a gate is not a thing his body can hold. Damage to that organ does not stop him working. It stops him being able to. The spoil around the seam is the only ground in the setting where waste does not disperse, because spatial law is unspent on the plains, so forty years of it lies where it was dropped. He certifies faces against it, and the certification is the most honest measurement taken anywhere on the flats, because the instrument is a body that has already paid.
history: Born on the flats below the Exhausted Seam to a line of face-readers, and put into a drift at eleven years old, because an ashwalker's first trade is breathing what the seam gives off.
Cleared the sixth vessel as a boy and became the youngest face-reader the guild had set on a face, which was entered as a record and then used as one.
Began loading spoil sacks out of the drift to pay a family debt to the heap crews, and found the work kept his chest warm and his breath even in air that had already closed two men.
Took the reading post when the previous reader retired at the eighth rung and nobody replaced the reading, and discovered the post had no procedure because nobody who could do it had ever needed one.
Started counting his own breaths against the tally board this season, because the board is the only instrument on the seam that also counts him.

personality.summary: Exhaustively observant about air and incurably incurious about himself, carrying the specific guilt of a man who has made his own body the only tool in the room. He notices what a face will hold before he notices what his own chest is doing, and he has known for two seasons that the distinction is not neutral.
traits: names the air before he names the man
counts his own breaths out loud without noticing he has started
will not enter a face he has already certified once
answers questions about the seam in the seam's own vocabulary and refuses to translate it
treats his own body as an instrument kept on a shelf
mannerisms: pulls the mouth-cloth down and back up mid-sentence rather than between sentences
wipes his nostrils on the back of his wrist, checks the cloth, and goes on
sets a sack down at exactly the same distance from his boot every time
stands side-on with the nearer shoulder to the drift
taps two fingers against his sternum before saying a number, as though asking the organ whether it agrees
motivations: wants to be asked to certify his own face, because a refusal would be a second opinion
wants the seam's readings posted where the crews can read them, so his tally is not the only count
wants to reach the eighth vessel before the grit reaches the eighth vessel
wants to be replaced by somebody with a second pair of lungs
flaws: cannot read his own face and has stopped calling that procedural
has never told the guild that the board counts him as well as the face
will certify a face he should refuse, because refusing costs a crew a season and he is the only one who can pay the difference
believes his own reserve is a guild asset and has never asked whether it is
personality.voice: Short, technical, and inhaled halfway through every sentence. He speaks in durations rather than verdicts, and cannot stop adding the air condition to things that do not need it. To a layman he sounds like a man who cannot get a word out; he has simply never learned a shorter unit than a breath.
taboos: will not certify a face he has stood in for less than a full shift
will not take the mouth-cloth off inside the drift
will not let anyone read his tally board aloud but himself
refuses to be thanked for a reading he could not survive getting wrong

relationships.note: The last ordinary vessel and the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened, which is why the rung-8 gate costs twelve vessels and not thirteen. In an ashwalker it is also the first place the mineral load settles, so the gate he is refused at and the organ taking his payment are one organ, and his ceiling is a countdown rather than a target.

The lung governs the intake the whole ladder is built on, and an ashwalker's intake is grit rather than air. Damage there shows as shallow breath before it shows as weakness, so his lungs report late, and he reads other people's chests by a sign his own have never given him.

The guild exists because spatial law is unspent here, so forty years of heap must be carried out by hand before the face can advance a foot. It pays him a shift rate and asks for a reading, and it has never once asked what the reading costs.

Sterile spoil that has not moved in four decades, because nothing on the plains can carry it away. It is his workplace, his supply and the reason the seam is a ruin whose end outlives everyone who remembers the working.

Mortal repair work whose only improvement is iron, on a flat where every tool is consumed by clearing spoil rather than by making anything. The craft that would mend what the grit is doing to him is the same craft his shift is eating.

What the clan holds is a crew and a number on a public tally, because a weight is the only measurement two crews on a frame with no spatial law have ever agreed on. He certifies the face that decides which crew works, so his breath orders the tally.

A frame that agrees and nothing crosses is the standing puzzle about an inscription that matches and an effect that does not arrive. Voss is that puzzle given a wage: his body agrees perfectly with what a face should hold, and nothing crosses back out of him.

reference_stats.summary: Reads a body for what it can be made to endure, and endures more than anyone in the room while doing it. Treat him as an environment rather than a duellist. The question is never whether he wins a fight but how long he can stand in the air, and the answer is always longer than the fight.
strengths: Works an exposure that has closed softer bodies and reports from inside it rather than from a distance
Certifies a face better than anyone alive, because no rival can afford to be wrong at the same proximity
Holds seven ordinary vessels open on grit alone, which is a reserve nobody with cleaner intake can match
Carries a heavy load over bad ground without altering his gait, which makes him useful as a moving reference
weaknesses: The organ carrying his ceiling is the organ his work is loading, and the payment cannot be deferred
Cannot survive being moved. A body that has earned its post by standing still has nothing left for being carried
His own face is the one face on the seam he cannot read, and his instrument is his chest
Every advantage is bought with the intake that is shortening the span he has left to spend it in
reference_stats.combat_read: He does not fight in the open. He fights by remaining where a fight has already been decided to be survivable, and he wins by outlasting the refusal of the air rather than by striking. Anyone who can move him, or who can make him leave the drift, has already beaten him, because a face-reader carried off his face is a man with nothing left to measure.
notes: His tally counts two subjects and the second one is not written in the guild's column headings.
No stat line models a body whose limit and its livelihood are the same organ, and that absence is the design.

art.palette_notes: Ash grey and wet stone black carry the whole value range, with the bleached ochre of the guild seal as the only chromatic event. Ink line is heavy and slightly broken, closer to a working tool than to a portrait, and the light is a carried lantern from below, because this is a face lit from the bottom by the thing it is inspecting.

name: Sill Emberlack
aliases: the floor that cannot be entered

identity.realm: Mind path, walled and still. The warding is total and the floor it defends produces nothing, because elemental law is not written at the tier he is posted to.

appearance.presentation: A seated figure with more heat in the outline than in the face. He is dressed for an office rather than a body: the Held Hour supplied the linen, and the linen has not decided whether to smoulder. People who want to be frightened of him are mostly disappointed, because there is nothing on him to aim at.
appearance.age: Not determinable from the outside and not asked. A cinderkin body is authored where a world's elemental slot is written, and the ley has been writing the same slot for a long time.
appearance.build: Broad through the chest and strangely light everywhere else, with hands that are warm to the touch at a distance and give nothing back when held.
appearance.complexion: A dull ember-grey, darker at the joints and lighter along the forearms, with a faint bloom of heat that rises and falls with his attention rather than with his temperature.
appearance.hair: None, and a fine drift of grey ash at the crown that is his own and not the room's. It settles back down within seconds of anyone looking at it directly.
appearance.eyes: Pale and without a wet edge, reflecting the lamp rather than the person. They do not narrow, which is the first thing that unsettles visitors and the last thing they stop noticing.
appearance.palette: Ember grey, unbleached linen, and a single warm ochre at the throat. Almost the whole value range sits in the two greys, because a thing that produces nothing should not look as though it is about to.
appearance.attire: Unbleached linen over a plain wrap, hemmed once at the shoulder where the heat has crept, and soft-soled shoes worn out on one side. Nothing about the cut is a rank and everything about it is a decision somebody else made.
appearance.marks: A fine grey bloom across the forearms where the linen sits closest, and no other marking at all, which visitors find more unnerving than a scar would be.
appearance.bearing: Perfectly upright when seated and entirely unmoving when not, with the particular stillness of something that has no reason to spend effort on being noticed.

canon.role_in_story: The Held Hour's standing proof. The assembly tends the floor during the hour nobody is permitted to explain, and its only control is that nothing happens during that hour; Emberlack is the body that makes that visible. He was posted three hundred measures below the ley that authored him, because the floor needed a proof and a proof does not have to be useful. Six years on, nobody has put that in writing.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in the bare antechamber of the Held Hour with his hands open on his knees and an untouched cup of water on the floor beside him, having sat through the whole unexplained hour, answering when spoken to that he had not been asked to do anything at all.
canon.lore: A cinderkin is an elemental body that needs a slot in a world's elemental law to exist at all, which is why that law is authored with a range rather than a switch: a world with no slot has no cinderkin, and a world that spends its slot on cold produces a different body entirely. Below the Ember Ley the elemental group is unspent, and an unwritten group has three signatures, no process, no substance and no licensed life form, so an elemental technique runs at full strength there and produces nothing whatsoever. That is not a weakened cinderkin. It is a body working perfectly in a room with no chemistry for a product. His warding is the flattest surface on the terrace, because Still Water leaves an incoming impression nothing to break against and Barrier Cultivation trains the wall as a separate muscle, so an attack that arrives does not arrive. The floor he defends cannot be entered. Neither can it be used, and the office paying him has known that since the day he came and has never once said so in writing.
history: Authored in the Ember Ley's own fire, where the elemental slot of a world is written in heat, in the last generation that produced a cinderkin body at all.
Brought down the ley shaft to serve as an attendant at the Held Hour, on the doctrine that a being which cannot produce an effect is the safest possible guard.
Learned inside his first year that his element is not written at the tier he was posted to, said so once in the flat liturgy, and was not contradicted.
Asked, in his fourth year, whether he could produce anything at all, and answered that he could produce everything and that there was nothing here to produce it into.
Began recently to ask the hour's staff what the floor is actually defending, which is the first question he has asked that was not about himself.

personality.summary: Absolutely imperturbable and completely incurious about his own condition, right up until the question stopped being about himself. He was filed as a safety and spent six years as one, and the change in him is not a change of temperament. It is that he has begun to want to know what the safety is for.
traits: does not begin a sentence and has never needed to
answers exactly what was asked and never the thing behind it
reports his own output as nil with neither bitterness nor self-pity
is at ease in a room where nothing happens and visibly uneasy in one where something does
has begun keeping a list of what the floor has actually contained him against
mannerisms: sits with palms up and fingers loosely curled, the posture of something with nothing to hold
drinks nothing, because drinking is a process and the tier offers nothing to process
goes very still when surprised, which visitors read as calm and which is actually the warding reacting
speaks in the flat liturgy's cadence, one clause, no modulation
tilts his head toward a room rather than toward a person
motivations: wants to know what the floor is defending
wants his element written somewhere he is not, so the capability is not the whole reason he was sent
wants to be reassigned rather than dismissed, because reassignment is a measurement and dismissal is a judgment
wants somebody with standing to read the list he has started keeping
flaws: cannot tell an absence of threat apart from an absence of anything
accepted for six years that the office knows he produces nothing and never once made them write it
reports his own nil output honestly, and the honesty has been read as insubordination
cannot want a thing at full volume, which is precisely what the warding is for
personality.voice: Flat, unhurried, and almost entirely literal. He gives the number that was asked for and stops, so people believe he is withholding something. He has never managed to explain that there is nothing behind the number.
taboos: will not take an elemental shape below the ley, because there is nothing for the shape to be made of
will not describe his warding as protection, and will not describe it as anything else either
refuses to be inspected for effect, since an inspection of a nil returns a nil
will not be seated as a specimen

relationships.note: At the two elemental domains where elemental law is unspent, a technique at full strength produces nothing. That is the setting's most instructive ruin, and he is the living edge of it: the process is not failing, there is simply no product for it to have.

The one authored elemental is licensed only at the immortal and transcendent tiers and reaches a combat power nothing else in the setting approaches. Below the Ember Ley it is not a creature that is rare; it is a creature with no lawful existence at all, running at full strength and producing nothing.

It flattens the mind so an incoming impression has nothing to break against, and it is almost wholly unelemental because it does no damage to anybody. Everything he is professionally, he is because of a technique that was deliberately built to do nothing.

Mental defence and resistance to illusion are practised by deliberately having the wall struck. He is the only person on that floor who has had it struck every hour for six years, and he has never once been asked what the strikes were for.

The office tends the floor during the hour nobody is permitted to explain, and its work only counts if it is repeated. It repeated it with a body that could not be harmed, and never wrote down that the same body could not help, which is the entire content of his employment.
The hour is kept rather than the room, and he has kept it more reliably than anyone who was ever in danger during it, because there was never anything in it to be in danger from.

Three masters of the first breath is the standing question about who is credited with the intake a cultivation ladder is built on. A cinderkin is a being whose entire existence is a question of what it is permitted to breathe in, and who has never been credited for one.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot be entered, cannot be moved, and cannot be shown doing anything. Treat him as a room rather than an opponent: the fight is not against him, it is the long argument about what a floor is for, and he will still be sitting there when it finishes.
strengths: Flattens any incoming impression to the point of non-arrival, which no technique in the record counters because none of them is aimed
Holds a ward indefinitely, since there is no reservoir behind it that a long fight could empty
Cannot be impressed, threatened, bought or confused, because none of those are processes his element can carry
Is the only witness in the setting whose account of a hostile attempt is not in any way shaped by the attempt
weaknesses: Produces nothing. Every offensive reading of him is a reading of the tier rather than of him, and the tier owes him no product
Cannot be reassigned, cannot travel, and cannot be effective anywhere his element is unwritten, which is everywhere below the ley
Offers no evidence of any kind, so every claim made about him has to rest on somebody else's report
Six years of being a control has taught him that wanting things is expensive, which is the one thing he now needs
reference_stats.combat_read: He will not engage and cannot be engaged. Anyone who wants to be first has already lost the only thing he is standing there for. The only attack that touches him is procedural: get his element written into a frame, and the body that was harmless everywhere becomes the most dangerous thing on the floor.
notes: The capability and the unemployment are the same fact, and the record should not pretend there are two.
No stat line models a being whose output is structurally zero, and the empty column is the point.

art.palette_notes: Two greys carry everything, with a warm ochre at the throat as the only chromatic note and no highlight above bone value. Ink line is thin and even, with no shadow pass, because nothing in the picture is producing light and the drawing should not pretend otherwise. The lamp reflection sits in the eyes and nowhere else.

identity.realm: Mind path, girdling and heel vessels held without difficulty. The flank vessels never open, because they need two simultaneous pressure sources and his qi comes from one resonator.

appearance.presentation: A spare, patient man who looks like a clerk and is mistaken for a lamp. He has never once been in a room that was not within earshot of the object that made him, and the drawing gives him very little to indicate it, which is the point.
appearance.age: Indeterminate and recorded as indeterminate. The guild's own intake ledger files him by reference to the object's resonance rather than by a year.
appearance.build: Narrow and exact, with the shoulders of somebody who has carried nothing heavier than a ledger and joints that articulate very quietly.
appearance.complexion: Even and slightly translucent in thin light, closer to waxed paper than to flesh, and unweathered in a way people find difficult to explain and never pursue.
appearance.hair: Fine, colourless and kept flat, parted without a mirror because a mirror returns an answer he has never been given.
appearance.eyes: Pale and steady, with the particular fixity of a reader who is looking at something rather than through it. They do not blink at intervals; they blink when the resonance shifts.
appearance.palette: Ash, bone and one cold blue on the House's clasp. The range is narrow on purpose: he is one note and the drawing should not imply a chord.
appearance.attire: House grey, high-collared and close at the wrist, with the collar buttoned over the resonance scar at the base of the throat. Trousers plain, boots soft, and nothing in the cut that would catch on a corridor.
appearance.marks: A fine raised seam at the base of the throat where the sealed population was closed onto the object, and it is the only mark on him and it is never uncovered indoors.
appearance.bearing: Upright and unhurried, with a very slight habitual turn of the head toward whatever in the room is resonating, which visitors read as a tic and which is a compass.

canon.role_in_story: The Quiet House's continuous reader: one mind that can hold one reading for four hundred years without tiring and cannot hold anything else. The House uses him to watch a thing it refuses to name, which is the only arrangement that suits both a house that files nothing and a reader who cannot compare.
canon.first_appearance: First seen seated inside the Quiet House's unswitched chamber with his eyes open on a fixed point in the wall, answering after a pause of several seconds that he had been reading the same page since the last century changed and would not know whether that was correct.
canon.lore: A vaultborn population was sealed inside an object and has been answering that object's resonance ever since. Their qi comes from one resonator, so they hold the girdling and heel vessels without difficulty and stall at the flank vessels, which need two simultaneous pressure sources and they have one. That is the whole anatomy of this character: a mind of perfect and unfailing concentration that is structurally unable to hold a second impression at the same time. The extraordinary vessels open in a pair at the rung-14 gate, the yin and yang qiao authored together and crossed together or not at all, so the pair is the gate's entire content. Remove the object and they stop. Nothing else in the record is that completely non-portable, and the Quiet House, which takes discretion as payment for teaching, is the only employer in the setting that does not need him to go anywhere.
history: Sealed into the vault as an infant with a generation nobody can now name, in the year the extraction guild took its charter over the object.
Grew to full stature inside the resonance and has never been further from the vault floor than a corridor he could walk.
Cleared the girdling and heel vessels early, which the guild's wardens recorded as unremarkable and which is in fact the entire ceiling.
Was contracted out to the Quiet House by a guild officer who wanted the reading kept and could not say whose reading it was.
Began this season to be asked to look at two things at once, and has declined four times without offering a reason.

personality.summary: Unfluctuating, unbothered, and privately aware that his usefulness is a function of a defect. He has never been tired and has never been surprised, and the second has cost him more than the first, because a man who cannot hold two things at once cannot tell you that something changed.
traits: answers only once the whole question has been asked, because he cannot hold half of one
never varies in tone across a conversation or across the decades of them
does not interrupt, and does not appear to notice being interrupted
records what he reads and nothing anybody has said to him about it
declines compound requests without explanation and without irritation
mannerisms: orients his head very slightly toward whatever is resonating and toward nothing else
closes his eyes to read and opens them to answer, as though the two are separate acts
repeats a question's exact wording before answering it, never its meaning
sits with the soles of his feet flat and does not shift weight for hours
stops mid-gesture when anything in the room changes pitch, and resumes exactly where he was
motivations: wants to be asked to hold two things at once, because the refusal is the only evidence he has of a limit he cannot feel
wants the reading he keeps named in a document he is permitted to see
wants somebody with a comparison to tell him whether anything has changed
wants to leave the resonance, which he will not say aloud
flaws: cannot notice a substitution, because noticing one requires two impressions and he is built for one
reports the reading as steady whether or not it is, because steadiness is the only property he can attest to
has never contradicted anybody, having no mechanism for holding a contradiction alongside the claim
cannot describe his own condition to a rescuer, because describing it would need two frames at once
personality.voice: Level, unhurried and slightly delayed, as though the sentence must be finished being assembled elsewhere before it arrives. He restates questions word for word. People read the pause as calculation; it is a gate he has to pass one item at a time.
taboos: will not hold two readings in parallel and will not pretend to
will not leave the object's resonance, on any terms including his own
will not sign that a reading is unchanged, since he can attest only that his own attention was
refuses to guess at a comparison

relationships.note: The single resonator his population draws qi from, held under the extraction guild's charter and described only by those already answering it. It reads as a law imprint held at one value, which is why it is recorded as resembling one and never as being one, and settling it would need an observation made from outside its own resonance, the one thing a vaultborn cannot do.

It opens at the rung-14 gate with its yang counterpart and is the first of the extraordinary vessels to serve motion rather than storage. The two are authored as a pair, crossed together or not at all, so the pair is the gate's entire content and he has only ever been able to open one side of it.

They hold the girdling and heel vessels without difficulty and stall at the flank vessels, which need two simultaneous pressure sources and they have one. His single source is the reason his attention never drifts and the reason it cannot widen, and both facts are downstream of the same number.

Caging a forming core in iron is the one craft the mortal tier is trusted with, and the knowledge is intact while the ore is not. His entire population is the living demonstration that the cage worked and that the supply, not the method, is what failed.

The House publishes teaching and takes discretion in return, and it rivals the Saltledger over who may keep a record. A reader who cannot compare and cannot leave is the only kind of keeper a house that files nothing can safely hire.

A longmarrow and a stoneborn claim the same seniority by different rules, and the dispute is only decidable by a reading both sides accept. His is accepted by both, because it is the only reading neither has ever thought to doubt.

The Ash Vault keeps an unbroken shell and writes the whole recovery down in public, never displaying the fragments again. The House answers the same question with a reader who holds one impression forever and tells nobody what became of it, and the two answers are durable for exactly opposite reasons.

reference_stats.summary: Holds one reading perfectly, for as long as anyone cares to keep asking, and cannot hold a second one at all. Treat him as an instrument with one input. Nothing he does scales, nothing he does drifts, and nothing he does can be compared with anything.
strengths: Attention that does not wander across a span that would exhaust any organic reader in an afternoon
Cannot be lied to by a display, because he is reading the source and not the presentation
Immune to fatigue, distraction, boredom and flattery, none of which are processes his qi has a channel for
The most reliable continuous record in the setting, since nothing about him can change while he is holding it
weaknesses: Cannot hold two impressions at once, which removes comparison, contradiction, suspicion and corroboration
Cannot leave the resonance, so every capability is jurisdictionally limited to one object
Cannot report a change, only the absence of one in himself, which is a much weaker claim than it sounds
Cannot be rescued, describe his condition, or be told what is wrong with him in terms he would accept
reference_stats.combat_read: He does not fight and is not fought. Any technique that needs two things at once passes a being who has room for one, and any opponent who establishes a second reading wins instantly, because a single tone cannot hear a wrong note and detecting one requires hearing two. The duel is not with him; it is with the arrangement that keeps him in one room.
notes: His defect and his value are the same organ, which is the only honest way to write him.
No stat line models attention that cannot widen, and the missing column is the character.

identity.realm: No path at all. An emberblood's mind closes once the furnace is lit and his body draws its fuel from itself, so he is not on a ladder, and the ladder was never the thing that was going to keep him alive.

appearance.presentation: A lean man who looks like everyone else's grandfather and radiates like a stove banked for the morning. He is the only person on the plains whose face visibly runs warm, and he has stopped apologising for it in the last year, which is the most noticeable thing about him.
appearance.age: Middle by the arithmetic of his kind and old by the arithmetic of everybody else. A short-lived body that has been dosed rather than trained arrives at middle looking like a note in a margin.
appearance.build: Wiry, quick and slightly underfed, with hands that are warm to the touch through a household's winter wall and forearms that show the tremor of a reserve being spent at a controlled rate.
appearance.complexion: High colour and faintly translucent at the throat, with a heat flush that arrives and leaves on a rhythm he has learned to hide and can no longer fully hide.
appearance.hair: Iron grey at the temples, cropped for the heat, and singed short in one place above the left ear where a household's roof came down while he was under it.
appearance.eyes: Bright and quick, with a warm iris, and they go hard and still the moment he is asked how much is left.
appearance.palette: Furnace orange, ash grey and one bleached cloth white. The orange is in the skin rather than the clothes, because the fire in this record is structural and putting it in the costume would be a lie about where it lives.
appearance.attire: Loose bleached shirt and waistcoat open at the throat to shed heat, a dose satchel of oiled cloth across the body, and boots resoled twice by households that owed him and would not say so.
appearance.marks: A lattice of fine burn lines across both forearms, the record of a hundred doses administered to other people, and one hand with a scar through the palm from a cup he broke rather than let fall.
appearance.bearing: Forward-leaning and quick, the walk of somebody with somewhere to be before the window closes, and he stops dead in doorways so a household can get past him.

canon.role_in_story: The last working copy of the Cinder Famine Dosage Tables, and the reason the tables stopped being a schedule and became a supply. A dose is measured in bodies rather than in measures, because the body being dosed is the substance being administered, and he is the entry that has not yet been spent.
canon.first_appearance: First seen sitting on a low stone outside a plain household with a slate on his knees and his own hands laid flat across it, explaining that the table's next entry needs one reserve's worth of fuel and that he is the entry, and that the table has no other column for it.
canon.lore: A fire-affinity body with no elemental law seated beneath it has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve, so the fastest race in the setting was at once the shortest-lived and the most dominant, and the famine that thinned them was the demographic shape of that arithmetic rather than a catastrophe that happened to them. Cultivation cannot repair it, because the reserve is the body and a body cannot be topped up. That arithmetic is why the dosage tables exist at all: dosing schedules for a population whose fuel was itself, kept by the households that had the tables and then ate the medicine first, so a bad grazing year became a medical shortage before it was a hunger, and the tables were consumed by the crisis they were written to answer. Braymark holds the copy that was not eaten. He practises nothing, because the mind closes once the furnace is lit and a body that is spending itself cannot also be learning.
history: Born on the plains after the thinning, into a household that had been given a table and had used the table on itself.
Learned the whole schedule by heart before he could read it, which is how a dosing plan survived a household that could no longer read.
Took a supply contract to move medicine rather than to receive it, on the reasoning that a man receiving medicine is a man whose reserve has already been counted by somebody else.
Watched three households administer the last of a batch correctly and lose two of the patients anyway, and began dosing on the arithmetic of the reserve rather than the arithmetic of the illness.
Started marking his own expenditure on the copy, in his own column, which is a column the table does not have.

personality.summary: Brisk, unsentimental, and running a private arithmetic that he shows to nobody. He is the most useful man on the plains and the only one whose usefulness is finite, and he has decided to be both facts at once rather than to manage either of them.
traits: answers any question about supply with a number and a window and nothing else
will not take medicine himself, and says so before being asked
keeps his own consumption in a column the table does not have
treats refusal as a dosing decision rather than as a moral one
talks about his own reserve in the future tense right up until the moment it is spent
mannerisms: wipes his palms on his thighs before touching anyone, a working habit picked up from people who handled grit and never explained
counts under his breath while a household argues, and stops the instant they agree
hands a wrapped dose over with both hands, like something being returned rather than given
checks an outer cuff for grit he has not been anywhere near
sits with his back to a wall and his knees apart, breathing slowly and visibly
motivations: wants the table held in more than one place
wants to be dosed before he is spent rather than afterwards
wants somebody with standing to insist on the reserve column
wants to be allowed to refuse without having to justify it
flaws: counts himself as stock and has never found a way to stop
will not say no, having never needed to, because the arithmetic supplies the refusal on his behalf
keeps the private column in the one place that cannot be audited, which is his own head
cannot be persuaded that he is not also medicine
personality.voice: Fast, plain and counting. He talks in doses and windows and never in feelings, and he has been called cold by people who wanted to be told there was enough, which he could not do without lying about a column.
taboos: will not be administered a dose by anyone who has not read the table
will not take a household's last measure

relationships.note: A fire-affinity body with no elemental law beneath it burns its own reserve, so the population thinned at exactly the rate it could not stop. The dosing table exists because the fuel was the body, and every column of it is written in a currency that does not grow back.

The tables were kept by the households that had them and ate the medicine first, so a bad grazing year was a medical shortage before it was a hunger. His copy is the one that was not eaten, which makes him the last reader rather than a distinguished one.

The fastest refiner in the setting, running short, with the mind closing once the furnace is lit. Fire affinity is structural rather than a gift, which is exactly why the reserve can neither be trained up nor argued with.

It collapses a year of refined qi into one hard line, the sharpest thing a mortal hand can throw and the cheapest way to find out what metal overcomes. It is the perfect expression of a body whose fuel is itself, because it spends everything or nothing.

The one plant authored into all four world tiers at once, and so the spine of every economy between them. It is what a dose is made from, and it is the single good a mortal herbalist and an immortal alchemist can both trade in.

The society exists because a carrying culture that refused to publish a price list could not buy insurance, so it pooled liability by presence. He is that liability, and the only reason the pool has not been asked to pay twice is that his column is not on the sheet.

The scrub's herb is medicine, feed and famine at once, so a bad grazing year removes the medicine before it removes the hunger. Every dose he carries was grown in a field whose failure and the illness it treats are the same event.

reference_stats.summary: Hits harder than anyone on the plains for as long as there is anything left to hit with, and the something is him. Treat him as a finite weapon with a schedule. Every question about his strength is really a question about how much of the answer has already been used.
strengths: Refines faster than any body in the setting, because there is nothing to wait for and no budget above him to draw on
The first strike is the best strike, so an ambush is the worst possible way to meet him and a negotiation is the best

Carries the only uncorrupted schedule, which makes him the setting's authority on when a body has had enough
weaknesses: The resource is the body. Nothing restores it, no technique substitutes for it, and the shortfall arrives without any feeling that something is wrong
Cannot be sustained. A second exchange costs twice the first and is paid for out of the same column
Cannot be healed by an ordinary injury because an ordinary injury is the whole problem, so field medicine works only on him and only if it is a dose
Structurally uncultivated: the mind is closed and the body is spending, so there is no practice left to improve anything
reference_stats.combat_read: Everything he does is spent from a fixed total, and the shape of the fight is therefore a scheduling problem rather than a skill problem. Let the first exchange resolve on his terms and he has already spent the answer; stretch it past two exchanges and the man standing there is no longer the man who arrived. Beat him by making the fight last, which is the one thing he has no answer to.
notes: He is entered in his own table in a column that does not exist in the schedule, and that is the character.

identity.realm: Mind path, well advanced and by the setting's standards unhurried. A longmarrow cannot take the body path at all, because hardening the bone stops the turnover the memory runs on.

appearance.presentation: A very old man in a clerk's collar who does not look frail so much as unrevised. Everything about him has been maintained rather than replaced, and people who work with him find the maintenance harder to look at than the age would have been.
appearance.age: Old beyond the range his office admits to. He gives the same age as the chair, on the grounds that the chair is what has been in post longest.
appearance.build: Tall, extremely thin and slightly stooped at the upper back only, with hands that are all knuckle and a chest that moves very little when he breathes.
appearance.complexion: Pale and dry and paper-toned, with translucent skin at the temples and no weathering at all, because four centuries of a body whose qi lives in bone does not involve much sun.
appearance.hair: Thin, long, colourless and kept in a single unbound fall down his back, tied once at the nape with a cord he has had since before the present office existed.
appearance.eyes: Clear and pale blue and completely steady, with the particular fixity of a person who is not looking at you but at the position you are standing in.
appearance.palette: Bone, grey-white and one ink black at the collar. The range is narrow because his life has been one colour of work and the drawing should not imply variety.
appearance.attire: Notary grey, high-collared, belted at the waist rather than at the hip, with a reading stand carried under one arm everywhere he goes, including rooms where nothing is to be read.
appearance.marks: No scars and no weathering, and the absence of both is conspicuous on a body that has been in post since before the building was raised around it.
appearance.bearing: Very straight from the waist up, hands folded, and slow in the way a thing is slow when it has never in four hundred years needed to hurry out of a room.

canon.role_in_story: The Nine Seat Notary's precedent: the one officer who can say what the office has always done, which is the only evidence available for anything the office is about to do again. Every question at the terrace that asks what a seat has permitted before is answered out of him, and he is the only witness in the setting that cannot be cross-examined, because he will not give it as testimony.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the terrace reciting, without any visible reference, the terms on which a vacancy was once left standing, and stopping in the middle of the recitation to say that the reading was from memory and that memory was the only copy still in existence.
canon.lore: A longmarrow's qi is stored in bone that turns over at about a percent a year, so the race lives four centuries and thinks in lengths nobody else can hold, and the setting's only durable library is a single body. It is also why they cannot take the body path: hardening the bone stops the turnover the memory runs on, so the longest-lived body in the record is built out of the one material it may never stop replacing. Ninefold is the Notary's precedent, and a precedent is the cheapest evidence in the setting because it never has to be proved twice. His reserve sits in the bladder, the one ordinary vessel whose authored tier lies inside the mortal band while its work is bookkeeping rather than strength; it holds what the body has decided not to spend, and damage there does not cripple. It exhausts, quietly and last, which is exactly why a four-hundred-year office has never noticed.
history: Born into the Notary's clerks' line, in the generation already reading precedents aloud to the seats.

Cleared the girdling and heel vessels and, unusually, held the position of reader for sixty years without ever attempting the body path, which the office recorded as a preference and his line recorded as arithmetic.
Inherited the position of precedent from a predecessor who died between two hearings, having read the standing terms that morning without knowing it was the last time.
Began answering the terrace's questions from memory alone after the chamber archive was consolidated, which saved the office a clerk and cost him the only thing that could have checked him.
Has said nothing about his own condition for some years, on the reasoning that a precedent is not evidence about himself.

personality.summary: Serene, unhurried, and privately certain in a way that has quietly stopped being checked. He is the most reliable witness the terrace has and the least supervised, because what he provides is by definition what the office has done before, and what the office has done before is what he provides.
traits: answers in the office's own vocabulary and never translates it
takes a full minute before a long answer, because he is checking nothing and simply continuing
never volunteers, on the grounds that a volunteer has no standing
corrects a questioner's phrasing before answering it, gently and without exception
has not mentioned his own condition to anyone in some years
mannerisms: reads with his fingertips resting on his own sternum, feeling the beat as a metronome
closes his eyes for the last third of a long recitation and does not lose the place
speaks a given clause exactly the same way every time he has ever said it
sits with his back very straight and his hands folded, and does not move them for an hour
stops entirely, mid-answer, when the light changes, and resumes from the same word
motivations: wants the precedent written down while he can still say it aloud
wants to be examined by somebody with standing, having never been examined by anybody
wants the office to keep a copy, so that his declining is not a private matter
wants to be asked whether anything is wrong, and cannot bring himself to ask
flaws: cannot be checked, having arranged for the removal of the only thing that could check him
treats his own memory as an archive rather than as a body
has answered a question once and will give the same answer again, correctly, whatever has changed since
cannot distinguish the longest part of his life from the part that is failing
personality.voice: Slow, formal and enormously calm, with no trace of hurry and no trace of complaint. He uses the office's whole vocabulary precisely, and people who do not know it hear authority where there is only a very old person reciting. There is no point in his delivery at which a listener could tell whether it has changed.
taboos: will not answer a question in the plain words of the asker
will not speculate about whether the office was right
will not accept a written copy of his own recitation as the record
will not discuss his own future, on the grounds that a precedent is not a prophecy

relationships.note: A population that keeps its archive in one body turning over at about a percent a year and living four centuries, and cannot take the body path because hardening the bone stops the turnover. He is the durable library, and that is also why the office has never had to ask him to leave.

The one ordinary vessel whose authored tier sits inside the mortal band while its work is bookkeeping rather than strength; it holds what the body has decided not to spend. Damage there does not cripple, it exhausts, quietly and last, which is why it goes unreported for years.

The vessel every tradition on every path treats as the one that stores what refinement is for later, and the reason the ladder has an order at all. His four centuries of retention are that one organ's work, which is why he can hold a chain of cause and cannot put it down.

Their qi is stored in bone that turns over at about a percent a year, so they live four centuries and cannot take the body path at all. The setting's longest-lived body is built out of the one material it may never stop replacing.

The office names the unfilled high seats and is forbidden to take them, because four vacant seats were very nearly filled by decree. A precedent-keeper is what keeps that from being a formality: he is the reason a seat cannot be filled on the strength of a new reading.

The mystery is an office with a cost nobody has ever identified. Ninefold is the standing answer, because he can recite every arrangement the terrace has ever tried and cannot recite one that has not been tried, and neither of those is the same as being paid.

The Reader's Shelf is where a decision stops being an opinion. Everything on it came out of a longmarrow's mouth, and the shelf's authority is exactly the authority of the people who remembered to listen.

The oath forbids the answer rather than demanding it, which is the one discipline his memory is genuinely good at: four centuries of holding a thing he is forbidden to say, and no evidence anywhere in the record that the strain shows.

reference_stats.summary: Cannot be hurried, cannot be rattled, and cannot be shown to be wrong by anything a person in a room can do. Treat him as an archive with a mouth. The fight is not against him, it is against the fact that nothing in the setting has ever cross-examined him, and that is a fight with an institution rather than a body.
strengths: Holds a chain of cause across four centuries with no loss at the far end, which no other testimony in the setting can match
Cannot be fatigued, flustered, bribed or overawed, having no reserve that a long day could empty
Reads a room's history off its own wording without any preparation, because he is the room's history
His word carries the weight of an unbroken chain, which makes one sentence of his worth a year of argument
weaknesses: The organ holding his reserve exhausts rather than cripples, so the failure arrives quietly and last and has already been happening
Cannot be cross-examined in any useful sense, because answering in the plain words of the asker is a thing he will not do
Gives the same answer to the same question forever, correctly, including after the world has changed underneath the question
Has no institutional counterweight of any kind, having arranged for the only copy that could check him to be consolidated away
reference_stats.combat_read: He does not fight and cannot be fought, in the sense that matters here. Any attack lands on a man who will rise later and recite the attack, correctly, as though it had been argued. The only thing that defeats him is procedural: get somebody to cross-examine him with a comparison he has to hold at the same time, which is the one thing his four centuries were never built for.
notes: His function and his failure are in the same vessel, and writing them as two separate weaknesses would be the easy way and the wrong one.
No stat line models a resource that spends quietly, and the missing exhaustion entry is the design.

name: Wren Saltrill
aliases: the courier who has not been sent

identity.realm: Mind path, the eighth seat held and the ninth refused her on a salt-head. A brinecaller reads two chemistries through one kidney and cannot choose between them, so every sitting that asks for two conclusions at once costs her a day of headache. The Reach's method for the ninth seat is in her hands and the ninth seat's tolerance is not, and she has stopped calling that gap small.

appearance.presentation: She is written into a crossing rather than into a body. The Reach keeps her at the waterline because a brinecaller is the only frame in the record that can stand on both chemistries at once, and it needs one person on the line who is not a ritual, a credential or a tariff.
appearance.age: Midlife for a salted parent and young for the cross, which matures slower on fresh water than on brine and which inherits the salt parent's ceiling without gaining a step for having widened the map.
appearance.build: A saltfolk frame with the sac shallowed by the crossing and the limbs still shortened by a parent that could not leave the pan: broad through the chest and shoulders, short in the leg, and heavier above the waist than below it.
appearance.complexion: Sallow and salt-cured, with a fine white bloom across the shoulders and collarbone that reads as frost in low light and as scale under a hand.
appearance.hair: Wet-dark and cropped level at the jaw so it cannot hold brine, because hair that has taken salt is a wick and she works over open water.
appearance.eyes: Wide-set and slow to blink, with a film that comes up over them when she is choosing between two readings. The saltfolk range is narrow, so she reads concentration and not identity, and she has told people that exactly once.
appearance.palette: Brine green, wet slate, and one bleached white on the reach's waterline cord. The whole range is cold and the only warmth in the picture is the ochre of a lamp carried low, which is the light she reads by.
appearance.attire: A reach coat of oiled sail with a weighted hem, sleeves cut above the elbow so her forearms can be read for salt bloom at a glance, and a bleached cord at the throat that the waterline clerk ties and the wearer may not.
appearance.marks: White bloom over both shoulders, a pale band at each wrist where the cord sits, and an old split across the palm from a hull that heaved in a direction she could not correct for.
appearance.bearing: Squared to the water and never to the room, weight on the downhill foot, and one hand always resting on the line she is standing between, so that anybody who wants to move her has to say so out loud in front of the water.

canon.role_in_story: The Brine Reach's undemonstrated crossing. She is the only body in the setting that can walk out of a pan and onto a watered shore with no cut, no credential and no rite, and the Reach has therefore arranged for her never to do it in front of anybody. An underwriter priced her as a carrier and a counting house priced her as evidence, and the second price is the one falling. She is employed to remain plausible and never to be demonstrated, which is a post nobody can be retired from, because the demonstration is the only thing that would end it.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the reach's waterline cord with one boot wet higher than the other, taking a reading off a sill that had been cut for somebody else's tide table, while two clerks standing on opposite banks arrived at the same number by different routes and refused to agree about the residue.
canon.lore: A brinecaller is the crossing between a people that cannot leave the pan and a people that cannot leave the water, and it is the only body in the record that reads two chemistries in one kidney and takes its sense from both. That is range, not power: it carries the salt parent's split penetrating vessel unchanged, so the crossing widened where the body can go and left the ceiling exactly where the parent had it, which is the whole of what her employment is worth and the whole of what it is not worth. The far side of the one tear that has stood open writes the same law group at the same value, so by the setting's own rule it should be reachable, and no qi tide has ever crossed it, because a cycle that never arrives is not a cycle that is weak. She is the obvious courier for that crossing and the Reach knows it, so the Reach feeds her, houses her, and keeps her demonstrably unable to commit to anything. Her cultivation is the mind path, which is the only thing a body this deliberately unspecialised can do well: two readings held open at once, which is what the ninth seat asks for and what costs her a day of headache she pays without complaint, because the alternative is being asked to hold one. The salt-head cannot be trained out. It is the reason two salts are indistinguishable to her, the reason her name on a manifest is worth more than her body on a deck, and the reason nobody has ever sent her.
history: Born ashore to a salted parent and a watered one, on the estuary where both chemistries are within reach, which is the only ground on which the crossing is not a curiosity to be written down.
Took work as a line-reader for the waterline cord at fourteen, which is the trade that trains a brinecaller to hold two readings and to invoice for one.
Held a miscut sill for a whole season and returned a number the two houses would not both sign, which is the only published work of hers and is signed by neither.
Was priced twice inside one week, a carrier by an underwriter and evidence by a counting house, and has been the subject of both prices since without being told either figure.

Refused, this season, the one crossing that would have settled the tear, on the ground that a demonstration ends a post, and has not been able to explain the refusal to anybody who was not already owed an answer.

personality.summary: Precise about water and incurably vague about herself, carrying the specific shame of a woman who knows her own market value better than she knows her own name. She can call the concentration of a basin at a glance and cannot say how she feels about being kept.
traits: names a water before she names a person, and catches herself doing it
reads two samples at once and reports one of them, on principle
answers a question about the crossing in the crossing's own arithmetic
will not put a boot in front of the cord on either side
keeps a written account of the things she has not been asked to do
mannerisms: wets one boot and lets the other dry, testing which bank she is standing on
holds a sample up to the lamp and turns it instead of swirling it
answers a half-beat late, while choosing which of two truths to give
wipes salt bloom off her forearm with the back of her hand and checks the sleeve afterwards
steps back off the line before anybody else steps onto it
motivations: wants the ninth seat, and wants it more than she wants to keep the post
wants the sill table corrected in public so the two houses stop pricing her against different numbers
wants the tear's question answered by somebody other than herself, having priced herself as the answer
wants her name on a manifest to mean something before she is forty
wants the cord untied at her throat by a clerk rather than by a buyer
flaws: has never been sent and cannot say whether that is protection or a career she chose
quotes her own market value accurately when angry and does not notice she is doing it
cannot choose between two true readings and has made a habit of asking which one pays
will not demonstrate, which is indistinguishable from refusing, and lets the distinction stand
has never once asked the Reach what happens to her if the tear is answered by somebody else
personality.voice: Low, unhurried and permanently comparative. She talks in concentrations, gradients and differences rather than quantities, and will tell you what a thing is relative to before she tells you what it is. To a landsman she sounds evasive; she is describing the world in the only units in which two of its halves fit in one mouth.
taboos: will not drink on a shore she has not tested twice
will not sign a crossing that does not name the water on both sides
will not be weighed, measured or appraised in front of the party being appraised
will not take the cord off while somebody is still paying for her to stand behind it
refuses to tell a house what her crossing would cost, on the ground that the answer is the asset

relationships.note: The crossing made her the only body in the record that metabolises brine and fresh water alike, and gave her the best chemical sense in the setting and a ceiling the salt parent already had. Range is not power, and the whole of her post is what that sentence costs.

Two frames write one group at one value and no tide has crossed, because a cycle that never arrives is not a cycle that is weak. A body carrying both chemistries is the obvious courier for exactly that crossing, which is why the question carries a commercial stake nobody has been able to price and why she is the thing the stake is priced on.

Not a coast but an agreement: the far side of the one tear that has stayed open, named by the single group both frames write at the same value. She is the only living person who could stand on it without a rite, and she has never once been asked to try.

A tide is an authored law value moving through its range on a cycle, and every breakthrough in the setting is scheduled to one. Hers is scheduled to a tide nobody has ever observed arriving, which in her trade is the only kind of scheduling failure nobody is permitted to call a failure.

A coast whose temporal law was never written publishes its schedule against two tides a day instead of a calendar. She has read that table for eleven years and holds the one correction it has needed since the sill was recut, and publishing it would make the two houses agree, and the disagreement is what pays her.

A price stated once in the league's own channel is a price the kelp season cannot sustain, and every attempt to state one has become a war. The only carrier able to quote a price nobody else can hold for a whole season is her, and she is forbidden to quote one, so the war continues and she continues to be the reason it could not be won.

reference_stats.summary: Reads a body of water the way other people read a face, and is close to useless on dry land. The question is never whether she wins a fight but what the tide has been doing to the ground under both of them, because that answer settles the fight before either of them moves.
strengths: The best chemical sense in the record, and the only body that can take a reading on either bank of a shoreline without a rite
Holds two conclusions open at once and pays for the second one in a day of headache she has never once complained of
Carries the setting's only natural argument that the far shore is reachable, which nobody can disprove without sending her
Refuses to demonstrate, which makes her the most reliable witness in the setting to the fact that nothing has ever been demonstrated
weaknesses: Range is not power: the crossing widened her map and left the salt parent's ceiling where it was
Above the brine line a deepsalt simply stops, and she is not a deepsalt, but the basin still sets the terms of every season she works
Cannot be moved. An asset kept at the waterline is only an asset while the waterline holds, and hers is a claim rather than a fact
Her entire worth depends on a question staying open, so every party that wants her useful has an interest in her never being used
reference_stats.combat_read: She does not fight. She reads the ground and the water and gives the answer to whoever asked in time to act on it, and the ground is doing most of the work. An opponent who takes her off the shoreline has neutralised the only thing she is; one who waits for the tide has already lost to the part of her that keeps time.
notes: No stat line models a body whose asset is a question nobody has asked her to answer, and that absence is the design.
A split tally is reproducible only by two people who were both present. She is one of the few living people who can stand on both banks, which is the nearest thing in the setting to being both.

art.palette_notes: Brine green and wet slate carry the whole value range, cold and low-contrast, with the bleached white of the waterline cord as the only hard accent and a lamp ochre from below as the only warmth. Ink line is thin and wet, closer to a pen kept in salt air than to a brush, and the light is a lamp held low because that is the light she reads by and she is always shown reading.

identity.realm: Mind path, with the ceiling being a decision rather than an obstruction. Emberblood refines faster than anything recorded and an unlit furnace makes a mind do the work qi would otherwise do, so he holds the highest throughput in the setting on no fire at all. Every gate past the one he is standing on is reachable by spending reserve he does not have and has sworn not to burn, so his rate is the fastest available anywhere and his ceiling is the ceiling of a man who will not.

appearance.presentation: He is a demonstration that has outlived its argument. The Order points at him because nothing in the setting refines faster and nothing in the setting reads more sharply while refusing to spend, and he is cited by a discipline whose own teaching is that you should.
appearance.age: Young for an emberblood and old for a practitioner. The furnace that makes the body fast also shortens it, the Quenchbound house signs every child to a fifty-year estimate, and he is the only signatory on his own estimate still alive.
appearance.build: Lean to the point of difficulty, hard-shouldered, with the habit of holding heat in the chest and giving very little of it to the limbs.
appearance.complexion: Hot and dry, flushed across the cheekbones and the bridge of the nose, with heat-bloom patches on the forearms that come and go with how hard he is working.
appearance.hair: Black and cropped short for heat, singed shorter at the temples than at the back because he puts his head in his hands when a reading goes badly.
appearance.eyes: Bright, reddened at the rims, with a pupil that narrows on light and does not narrow on anything else at all.
appearance.palette: Charcoal black, ember orange at the throat and inside the sleeves, and one unburnt white at the collar. The heat is the only light in the picture and it is under his clothes.
appearance.attire: A Quenchbound coat of scorched wool, high-collared and laced to the throat, sleeves doubled and worn open at the cuffs because the heat has to go somewhere, and a signature band at the left wrist that is the only paper he carries.
appearance.marks: Heat-bloom on both forearms and across the back of the left hand, a burn scar at the right wrist in the shape of a seal that did not finish setting, and the singed gap at the temples.
appearance.bearing: Upright and very still, hands kept low and open, with a habit of turning his shoulder away from an open flame rather than toward the room.

canon.role_in_story: The Quench Order's standing refutation, cited by people who teach deliberate spending against the one practitioner in the setting who has never spent anything. He refines faster than any body on record and reads at the speed of a struck match, and he has never once lit his furnace, because lighting it closes the mind path permanently. He is therefore both the discipline's proof that the discipline is necessary and the evidence that it might be optional, and the Order has spent thirty years asking him to be one or the other.
canon.first_appearance: First seen in a public reading room with his furnace cold and his signature band showing, turning down the offered rate of a lit body by reading an entire sitting faster than the offer took to make, and then staying behind after the room emptied to correct the transcription, which was the only part of the performance nobody had paid for.
canon.lore: An emberblood body runs hot and short. Fire affinity is structural rather than a gift, refinement is faster here than anywhere in the record, and the span is measured in decades rather than centuries. It also carries the setting's sharpest conditional: the mind path closes permanently the moment the furnace is lit, so the fastest body available is a body whose greatest asset sits one act away from permanent forfeiture. That is arithmetic, not metaphor. The Quench Order teaches deliberate spending before a furnace overflows, and its reasoning is sound, because there is no seated elemental law in the mortal tier to spend into and every overflow has to be absorbed by flesh that cannot be repaired. Kindlefoot is the case that makes the rule visible. He sits on the highest throughput in the setting and reads faster than a struck match, and he has declined by name and in writing eleven offers to light. What he holds is not restraint but a method: on an unlit furnace the mind does the work the qi would have done, which is the entire reason his path is the mind path and not the qi path. The Quenchbound house signs every child to a furnace before it is named, and a signature is the only inheritance that survives a body which will not, so the band at his wrist is a document about his death that somebody else will have to keep. His authority is older and worse than that. He holds the only legible hand on the first fuel rationing, one of three names attached to a count that no two records place in the same place on the same day, and the title attached to the hand appears one event after the census that required it, which is late enough for an office to be manufactured and early enough for a person to be told to obey it. He is cited by a discipline that says spend deliberately, by people who have never met the only document that would settle who signed it.
history: Signed to a furnace in the Quenchbound house before he was named, and given a fifty-year estimate by an aunt who had signed two siblings and buried one of them inside it.
Worked out at twelve that an unlit furnace makes a better mind than a lit one makes a fighter, which is the only fact the Order would teach and would not pay for.
Cleared the reading-room benches in a single sitting at nineteen, cold, and turned down the lit body's rate in front of the house that had trained him.
Inherited the only legible hand on the first fuel rationing and found two other names already attached to the same count, in different places and on different days.
Refused eleven lit offers this year, in writing, and began keeping the refusals in a book, on the grounds that a refusal nobody can read is a rumour.

personality.summary: Exact about a thing he will not do, and privately furious that the discipline which taught him the cost now borrows his body as evidence. He is superb in front of an audience and worst alone with a page of his own handwriting.
traits: names the price of a technique before he says whether he likes it
will not discuss his own ceiling as a hardship, because a hardship can be appealed
keeps a written record of refusals and reads it back when he is contradicted
answers a question about the past with a document and a question about the future with arithmetic
treats being cited as a debt he did not sign
mannerisms: holds both hands low and open as though proving they are cold
turns his shoulder away from every open flame in a room
touches the signature band at his left wrist before agreeing to anything
blows once on his fingertips, uselessly, when a reading runs long
stops moving entirely while he is being cited, which is the only visible sign that he heard
motivations: wants the rationing count settled to a single hand so the discipline can stop borrowing his body
wants the ninth seat on a cold furnace, which nobody has recorded as possible
wants the eleven refusals read aloud by somebody who is not him
wants to outlive the estimate written into his own signature
wants to be asked what he is rather than what he is worth
flaws: has made refusal an identity and can no longer tell which refusals are principles
will not take a lit offer, which is indistinguishable from refusing to want anything
lets the Order cite him, because correcting it would require arguing that he is faster warm, which he has never tested
has not attempted to meet either of the other two names on the rationing count and will not discuss why
personality.voice: Fast, clipped and priced. He answers in cost and rate before feeling, interrupts himself to correct a number, and treats any question about his own future as a question about somebody else's estimate. To a beginner he sounds cruel; to the Order he sounds like a ledger that has learned to speak.
taboos: will not light a furnace to win an argument
will not sign a document naming a body he has not read the estimate for
will not be measured by anybody holding the pen
refuses to be called patient, on the grounds that patience is a word for a body that is waiting
will not accept a gift he cannot name a rate for

relationships.note: Runs hot and short, refines faster than anything here, and reads intent at the speed of a struck match, at the cost of a lifespan in decades and a mind path that closes once the furnace is lit. Every clause in that trade-off is the reason he is cited and the reason he is dangerous to cite.

The discipline teaches deliberate spending and closes permanently the moment the body is lit, and he is the dispute's living exhibit: the one body fast enough to prove spending is unnecessary and disciplined enough to be the proof that it was never voluntary.

A discipline of bankers rather than a school of thought, teaching that a furnace should be spent before it overflows because flesh cannot be repaired. It cites him as its necessary example and he has never once corrected the citation, which is the arrangement that lets both of them keep their position.

A house that signs every child to a furnace before naming it, because a fire-affinity body with no seated elemental law has no budget to draw on and must burn its own reserve. The signature is the only inheritance that survives a body which will not, so the band at his wrist is a claim on him that outlives him by design.

Three names are attached to the first fuel rationing and no two records place them in the same place on the same day, while the master's title appears one event after the census that required it. He holds one of the three hands, which makes him the only person alive who could settle a question three offices still answer with different names.

The path he has spent a life protecting and declining to trade away. Because his throughput is the highest in the setting, his reach is the greatest available anywhere and his ceiling is entirely self-imposed, which makes him the setting's clearest argument that a limit and a decision are not the same kind of thing.

reference_stats.summary: Reads faster than anyone in the room and fights like a man who has decided the fight would cost more than it returns. He is the fastest sight available and the slowest commitment, and the distance between those two facts is the whole of how he fights.
strengths: Refines faster than any body on record and has done so on a cold furnace, so the throughput costs him nothing he cannot spare
