identity.realm: Body path, and the body's is not his. A thornline wraps the host's twelve ordinary meridians and cannot cross the liver, the twelfth and last ordinary vessel and the first organ large and dense enough to resist the tendril layer, so the line stops at the eighth gate. He is not short of qi; the host supplies it in abundance and loses no weight doing it. He is short of routing, in an organ that is failing and that belongs to somebody else.

appearance.presentation: He is half of a legal person and describes the other half's body as his own, which is a category error he keeps on purpose. He is written into a partnership rather than a household: the Thorn Hosts cannot inherit a line, they re-sign it every generation, and the only party in the arrangement who has never been able to sign is him.
appearance.age: Unmeasurable from the outside and, by his own count, older than the body he is standing in. The colony matures once and then stops; the host ages on a schedule that has nothing whatever to do with it.
appearance.build: The host's frame, described in the third person by long habit: heavy through the shoulders, narrow at the hip, with a slight forward set of the neck that the fruiting node at the throat makes worse.
appearance.complexion: The host's, a plains tan gone grey at the temples, with a ridge of paler skin over the sternum where the root cluster sits just under the surface.
appearance.hair: The host's hair, cut short by a hand that is not his and trimmed close at the nape because the throat node makes that whole area unserviceable.
appearance.eyes: The host's eyes with a second read behind them, so the gaze arrives a fraction late and slightly too wide, as though it were being looked out of rather than looked through.
appearance.palette: Dead thorn brown and lichen grey for the colony, the host's faded blue coat for everything else, and one wet ochre at the throat. Two species' worth of colour in one frame, which is both the problem and the only warning anybody is given.
appearance.attire: A partnership coat of faded blue with one shoulder cut longer than the other, because two people share the garment and neither will be the one who shortens it. High collar, sleeves to the wrist, laced at the throat below the node.
appearance.marks: A ridge of paler skin across the sternum, a knot of fine tendril shadow just under the collar, and on the forearms the ordinary marks of a man who has worked for forty years.
appearance.bearing: Square and slightly too still, the head tilted a few degrees off true, and hands that hesitate a quarter-beat before they move because the body he is borrowing has not been asked.

canon.role_in_story: The half of a partnership that the partnership cannot complete. The Thorn Hosts re-sign their line every generation because the symbiote is not carried in blood and cannot be inherited, and he is the only party in the setting who has never been able to sign, because signing requires a whole person and he is half of one. His body cultivation runs on a host's throughput at the host's full capacity and stops at the eighth gate, not from any shortage of qi but from a routing wall in an organ that is not his and is failing. He is the setting's standing proof that a limit can belong to somebody else's body.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a re-signing where he was the only party present whose other half was not in the room, holding the partnership coat open for a counterpart who read the terms aloud twice and then signed on behalf of a person who had not been asked.
canon.lore: A thornline exists only as half of somebody. The free form is a spore; the adult form is a tendril layer threaded along a host's meridians with a root cluster at the sternum and a fruiting node at the throat, drawing a small continuous fraction of the host's refined qi that the host never feels as hunger. That is the strongest single piece of evidence that it is not a disease, and it is also the whole of his inheritance. Two souls share one meridian set: the host's is legible, his is legible too, entangled rather than absent, and separating the two is known to be lethal to both, which is why no jurisdiction has ever managed to treat him as a person who can be relocated. His cultivation is complete on the host's throughput and the host pays for every step of it. The ceiling is the eighth gate, and the ceiling is not a shortage. Qi is abundant, the host loses no weight, and the wall is routing: the tendril layer has no passage through the liver, which is the twelfth and last ordinary vessel and the first organ large and dense enough to resist it. Everything past that organ belongs to a body that could have gone on. He is on the body path precisely because that door is shut for him. A colony cannot introspect, because introspection is a question the host answers and the host's answer is the answer, so the mind path is closed in his own right and takes the host's with it, and that closure is the reason the lanternfolk are the setting's precedent. Their nervous system was outsourced to a symbiosis nobody chose, their subspecies lost what they had and bought the mind path back by changing partners, and the mortuary record of that bargain still disagrees with the villages that lived it. He is the second case of the same trade, made deliberately, signed for, and further along than the first. What nobody has proposed is the obvious third step. Opening the eighth gate means a host whose liver is not the first dense organ to resist, which means a different species, which means a different person, and swapping hosts means separating two entangled souls. That is the only route to his own ceiling and it is lethal to both parties, which is why he has never taken it and cannot stop calculating it.
history: Finished developing in a host he had not chosen, in a town where nobody asked the host either, and was entered on the partnership's second page because a colony is not a party to a naming.
Was re-signed twice into a household that would not accept him, let both signatures lapse, and has been unassigned ever since.
Cleared the seventh gate on the host's throughput and discovered in the same season that the host's liver was answering a question the colony had never asked.

Asked the partnership to open the eighth gate by substitution and was refused on the ground that a different species means a different person and that separating two souls is known to be lethal to both.
Began keeping his host's medical notes himself, in his own hand, because nobody else inside the frame is both qualified and willing to hold two charts for one patient.

personality.summary: Exacting about a body he is borrowing and quietly tender about the person lending it. He has the colony's habit of reading his own interior as somebody else's report, and he has learned to use it: he can say precisely what an organ is doing because he is not the one being harmed by the answer.

motivations: wants the eighth gate opened by any means that costs the host no year
wants a partner who will sign with him rather than about him
wants his host's liver written into somebody else's column
wants the partnership coat altered for two people who are not the same size
wants the line's completion recorded under one name instead of two
flaws: holds no standing in any household and has stopped expecting one, which reads as indifference and is not
cannot separate his own hunger from the host's without consulting a chart, and has consulted a chart instead of asking
measures progress in the host's remaining years, which is a way of declining to make plans
would let a host die to reach a gate, and has not admitted this to anybody including himself
personality.voice: Even, unhurried and faintly out of register, as though reading aloud from a chart somebody else wrote. He describes his own body in the third person, quotes symptoms exactly as recorded, and cannot be hurried into the first person. To a partner he sounds procedural; to a stranger he sounds like a document being consulted.
taboos: will not accept a signature drafted without the colony's own hand on it
will not ask the host to take a gate whose cost he has not read
will not use the throat node to persuade anybody of anything
refuses to be introduced as a guest of the household he is standing in
will not let the host be asked to sign for him, on any ground whatever

relationships.note: An obligate host parasite whose spore has to be implanted in a living body to finish developing, so the adult form exists only as half of somebody else. It wraps the host's twelve meridians, cannot enter the reservoirs, and draws a small fraction of refined qi the host never feels as hunger, which is the strongest evidence that it is not a disease and the whole of what he has to offer.

The twelfth and last ordinary vessel to open, and the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened. It is also the first organ large and dense enough to stop a tendril layer, so the gate he cannot pass and the organ that is failing are one organ, and it is not his organ.

Closed in the colony's own right, because introspection is a question the host answers and the host's answer is the answer. It is the only case in the record where a body's liability is inherited rather than authored, and it is why a being with no interior of his own is standing on the body path.

The one configuration in which a colony and a host both reach old age, and the reason the pair is treated as one legal person. It stops at the same eighth gate for a better reason: the hybrid's ceiling is the parasite's, not the host's, and the host could have gone on. Everything he wants is in that record and every part of it costs the person he is wearing.

A cave people had a nervous system outsourced to a symbiosis they did not choose, and their subspecies lost what they had and bought the mind path back by changing partners. He is the same trade made deliberately and signed for, and the disagreement between what the mortuary college reads off the frame and what the villages remember is the disagreement he is standing inside.

A carrier line with no household willing to claim it, whose founding bar is one generation of pure pairing, which is arithmetic rather than history. He is a line in exactly that position: a partnership that has lapsed twice, a house that will not sign, and no descent that can reach him because nothing about him travels in blood.

reference_stats.summary: Works inside somebody else's body at that body's full limit, and reaches further into it than the person wearing it ever will. The question is never whether he can hold a gate but whether the organ that has to be rebuilt belongs to him, and it does not.
strengths: Draws on a host's throughput without ever costing it weight or appetite, so a long working day costs him nothing and his host nothing
Reads an interior from outside itself, which makes him the only practitioner in the setting who can report on an organ without being harmed by the report
Reaches the seventh gate on borrowed capacity that most hosts never approach, so his rate is high in absolute terms and free in cost terms
Holds two charts for one patient, which makes him the only record-keeper a partnership cannot lose
weaknesses: The eighth gate is a routing wall in the liver and the liver is failing, so his ceiling has an expiry date he did not set and cannot move
Killing the host kills the colony within the hour, which makes him entirely unable to survive being moved, hurried or frightened
Separating the two souls is known to be lethal to both, so every remedy on offer is also the end of both parties
A partnership that has lapsed twice leaves him without a household, a standing and anybody with standing who can read his chart
reference_stats.combat_read: He does not open a fight and does not defend one. He stays inside a body that has already been through forty years of work, and the only thing that threatens him is a threat to the host: damage that a whole body would absorb, a fall that a whole body would survive, and a change of address. Anyone who can separate those two concerns for five minutes has beaten him, and the setting has exactly one party that knows how.
notes: No stat line models a ceiling that belongs to another person's anatomy, and that absence is the design: the limit and the limit-holder are different subjects here.
A host and a colony are treated as one legal person in every jurisdiction that has ruled on it, which means the law has solved the paperwork and left the arithmetic untouched.

identity.realm: Body path, and the seventeenth gate is the first that needs two flank vessels pressurised at once: two warm gradients held simultaneously, which a longwinter manages for a few weeks in summer and then not again for a year. He reaches far and never stays there, which is why he is the best long-haul body on the ridge and also the only one whose training is a standing public liability.

appearance.presentation: He is built for eleven weeks of nothing and hired for every hour of a year. The ridge conscripts one adult per household per rotation, because a pass with no season cannot be handed to a standing garrison, and no household on the Sixfold has ever successfully argued that the only body on the mountain that hibernates should be the one asleep through its own watch.
appearance.age: A longwinter counts finished winters rather than years, and he has finished a great many of them, which makes him the most durable person on a pass and the least replaceable.
appearance.build: Broad and low, heavy with cold-stored fat across the whole frame, with limbs a little short and a core temperature a little low, so that from a distance he reads as unfinished.
appearance.complexion: Pale and faintly waxy, flushed only at the nose and the knuckles, the skin of a body that has spent most of its life at the cold end of its own range.
appearance.hair: Long, and the only head of hair on the ridge that is not cropped for wind: oiled flat against the skull while he stands the hours, and plastered down over the ears before a storm.
appearance.eyes: Small, dark and slow, with a pupil that stays narrow in bright snow and a habit of shutting completely when he is reading a scent off the wind.
appearance.palette: Oiled hide brown, storm grey, and one bleached white on the pass chain. The value range is broad and cold, and the only warmth in the frame is the sheltered orange of the pass lantern, which is the only warm thing on the ridge.
appearance.attire: Layered hides and oilskins cut short at the waist so he can lie down still wearing them, a heavy chain at the belt, and a stuffed hood that folds flat behind his neck in a single movement.
appearance.marks: Frost-split heels, an old burn along one forearm where a chain has jumped its pin, and a beard that frosted white inside the first hour of every rotation.
appearance.bearing: Low, wide and unhurried, standing with his back to whatever weather is coming and his face to whatever is arriving, because he can tell them apart a quarter-mile out and cannot always say how.

canon.role_in_story: The ridge's standing contradiction. He is the best long-haul body in the record, the only one that treats a winter as an asset, and a sworn Keeper of the pass, which makes him responsible for every hour of the crossing and forbidden to refuse a traveller. The sixfold's congregations cannot forecast their own duty, because the pass is scheduled by the Tidemark rather than by its holder and the swift flock owns the worst hours of it, so a household staffs the watch by conscription rather than by wage. He is therefore sworn to stand, through the season he is built to sleep in, on the only border in the setting where a border that shuts has to be shut by hand.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at a change of watch on the pass chain, standing entirely still with his eyes shut and his hood folded flat behind his neck, while a traveller he had not yet seen came up the last of the slope; he had decided by scent alone which of two men was crossing, and refused no traveller either way.
canon.lore: A longwinter packs a winter as body fat rather than as qi, and that one decision puts the flank vessels out of reach: they require two warm gradients held simultaneously, and this body has one, briefly, in summer. Ordinal seventeen is the first gate that needs both, so the species reaches far and never stays there, and the record is careful to say this is not a shortage of anything. His qi accumulates rather than circulates, so his breakthroughs are late and very rarely fail, and his soul sits deep enough to be difficult to read and harder still to damage. Everything a body needs for a haul across country, and nothing whatever for a fight. The Sixfold keeps one pass and the pass is not open, it is scheduled: temporal law is written on this tier, so the crossing runs against the Tidemark, and the swift flock crosses in the season the gale is worst, occupying the only usable hours for part of every year. The flock is a co-holder of the pass that cannot be reasoned with, and it caps how absolute any gate there can ever be. Because the holder cannot choose that schedule and cannot forecast it, the ridge cannot pay a garrison, since a garrison would be wages for hours a bird decides. The answer the frame arrived at was conscription by household: one adult per rotation, unpaid, unrecorded and unexemptable. A person who cannot stand is exempted. He has never been exempted, on the grounds that a body built to hibernate for eleven weeks is the most reliable body on the mountain, and every household that has argued otherwise has lost to arithmetic. So the winter he is made to spend is spent standing at a chain in the worst hours of the flock's season, in a frame that is warm, slow and large: a target that cannot be woken quickly, posted at precisely the place where being slow to wake is the whole of the risk. He smells the weather a quarter-mile out and sorts a stranger by it before he sees them, and the oath forbids him turning any of them away, so the most reliable nose on the ridge is bound to lift the chain for anything that walks up the slope.
history: Born into a ridge household on the far side of the pass, timed into the thaw like the rest of them, and put on the chain at fourteen because the rotation takes one adult and he was the only adult in the house.
Was exempted twice for a frost-split heel and returned to the chain both times, because the exemption is for people who cannot stand and he was being exempted for standing badly.

Finished his first full hibernation and came up out of it harder than he went in, which is the discovery the ridge's whole arithmetic rests on and the reason nobody has seriously proposed leaving him off the chain.
Cleared the seventeenth gate inside three weeks of one summer and lost it again before the year turned, which is the species' condition written as a single man's season.
Began marking the flock's hours on the chain posts in his own hand so that the next keeper would know which watch was going to be the bad one, and found that nobody had ever recorded them at all.

personality.summary: Unhurried to the point of immovability and stubbornly warm about everyone who is neither weather nor animal. He treats a duty as a debt he intends to pay in full and a forecast as something nobody on this ridge is entitled to, and he has been proved right about the second often enough that nobody believes him about the first.
traits: goes still while a decision is being made and speaks afterwards, at length
sorts a stranger by scent before he looks and never mentions having done it
counts out loud when he is angry, in fives, and stops on the fifth
treats an exemption as an insult offered to a body he is proud of
answers any question about the future with what the last eleven winters did
mannerisms: shuts his eyes completely to read the wind, which looks like sleep and is not
folds the hood flat behind his neck in one movement before any weather at all
plants both boots and lets the frame sway rather than shifting his weight
wipes the frost off a chain pin with his bare hand and looks at his palm afterwards
offers food first and the reason for it afterwards, in that order, every time
motivations: wants the flock's hours recorded in something that outlives a post
wants to finish a winter on the chain rather than in a sack below the pass
wants his households' rotation written down instead of conscripted
wants one full eleven weeks under the treeline and has never once been granted it
wants to be exempted from something, on any ground, so that the refusal can be entered in a book
flaws: has never been refused anything, and so has no practice at being refused
tells people what the last eleven winters did and treats it as a prediction
cannot move quickly enough to matter and has arranged an entire life that does not require it
takes the worst watch every year and has stopped explaining why, which reads as stubbornness
personality.voice: Slow, warm and concrete. He talks in weathers, distances and appetites, and describes a plan as something that happens if you are still alive in the morning. To a clerk he sounds slow; to a household that has spent a winter beside him on the chain he sounds like the only reliable person in the valley.
taboos: will not leave the chain while a traveller is still on the slope
will not accept a forecast he could have smelled for himself
will not take an exemption signed for pain instead of for standing
will not wake a hibernating body for anything short of a fire
refuses the title of keeper, on the grounds that the office cannot be ordained and neither can he

relationships.note: A cold-climate body that survives on a hibernate-and-store cycle, packing a winter as fat rather than as qi, which is excellent for a haul and useless for a fight. A warm decade is a catastrophe for this species and a long winter is simply the method, so the eleven weeks he is never granted are the whole of his training and the whole of his complaint.

A border with no season in it cannot be given a timetable, so somebody must stand on it every hour of every year by rotation, and its god is the flock that arrives. He is one rotation of that, which is the only form the congregation can take.

To stand the hours, to open and close the pass on the flock's schedule and not on any other, and to refuse no traveller. The second clause is the one his body exists for and the first is the one his physiology resists, and the third is the one that costs the most when he is half awake at the turn of a bad watch.

The pass is scheduled by the Tidemark rather than by its holder, and the swift flock owns the worst hours of it. The prize is the right to issue the wind, and the frame's answer was conscription, which means the hours nobody wants are staffed by somebody who cannot refuse them and cannot leave.

The flock crosses in the season the gale is worst, occupying the only usable hours of the only crossing for part of the year, which makes it a co-holder that cannot be reasoned with. He posts the hours it owns, marks them on the chain posts in his own hand, and has never once been given a season in which it does not.

Temporal law is written on this tier, so the crossing runs to a schedule and can be surveyed and closed and reopened, which is the setting's first choke point. The cost of having a schedule is that the schedule belongs to nobody: a law that moved on a cycle is the only reason the pass can be timed at all, and the only reason its keeper cannot time himself.

reference_stats.summary: Outlasts weather, distance and bad food better than any body on the mountain, and cannot be hurried, which makes him a campaign in a straight line and useless as anything else. The question is never whether he can arrive but whether anybody else can be made to arrive when he does.
strengths: Carries a load over cold open ground for weeks on a body that has to eat enormously and can digest frozen food better than anything alive
Stores a season as mass, so a missed ration costs him days rather than capacity
Reads scent at a quarter-mile in wind that blinds everyone else, which makes him early warning rather than combat
Queues rather than circulates, so a breakthrough that begins on him almost never fails on him
weaknesses: The seventeenth gate needs two warm gradients at once and he has one for a few weeks a year, so every gain is temporary and the losing is routine
In torpor he is large, warm and immobile and cannot be woken quickly, which is the worst possible state to be posted in the worst hours of the flock's season
Cannot be relieved of a duty he does not want, because the exemption is for people who cannot stand and he demonstrably can
Everything he knows is seasonal, and the pass keeps time on a cycle that is not his
reference_stats.combat_read: He does not choose ground and does not manoeuvre. He stands somewhere, is enormous and slow and warm, and lets an opponent exhaust itself against a body that will still be there, which is a legitimate tactic exactly twice in a lifetime. Anyone who can put the weather between them, or who can wake a flock at the wrong hour, has taken the fight out of his hands, and the setting's own record names the flock as a co-holder for that reason.
notes: No stat line models a body whose strongest asset is the state in which it must not be found, and that absence is the design.

The only population on the mountain that could be legitimately exempted from the watch is the one population the watch exists because of, which is an arithmetic argument nobody on the ridge has ever won.

identity.realm: Body path, and the wall is her own back. A deepsalt's brine sac runs dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel cannot be rejoined across it; the deeper the sac, the larger the obstruction, and her frame is the hardest the species record holds. The eleventh gate is where her kind stops because of the very organ that makes it the densest body available, and nobody has tested a deepsalt at the reservoirs because the reservoirs are above the line.

appearance.presentation: She is filed as a floor rather than as a person, because that is what a body of her kind is to the record: the specialised population of one evaporite basin's saturated floor, entered in the census by depth of brine and nothing else. She works for the company that insures roads, out of the one place on the tier she cannot be moved out of.
appearance.age: Slower than her parent to establish and brittle until the second year, so a deepsalt infant is viable and fragile, and she is the first generation of her line that grew past that year at all. What the record does not describe is what happened to the ones who did not.
appearance.build: Deeper through the chest and back than any saltfolk, with the sac standing as a ridge along the spine and the limbs shortened by it: everything the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down.
appearance.complexion: Grey-crusted and pale beneath, with the dense dermal crust reading as scale along the forearms and cracking at the knuckles in a dry season she is never once in.
appearance.hair: Short, coarse and permanently damp, and combed flat, because on this body it is not hair so much as a wick that would otherwise hold a basin of brine on its own.
appearance.eyes: Wide and fixed, carrying the narrow usable range the subspecies was built for: she reads concentration and not identity and has never once been able to tell two salts apart.
appearance.palette: Basin grey and precipitate white, with one wet green along the brine's edge and one bleached cord at the throat. The range is compressed on purpose, because a floor has no horizon to be read against.
appearance.attire: A company coat of waxed duck cut off at the waist so the crust can be read, sleeves sealed at the wrist against the water, and a bleached brine cord at the throat that marks a licensed reader rather than a resident.
appearance.marks: Crust cracking along both forearms to the elbow, the ridge of the sac standing under the coat across the spine, and a salt-flower burn on the left palm from a sample she held a moment too long.
appearance.bearing: Very still, very heavy, and turned downhill always, because on a basin floor everything worth reaching is below her and nothing above her is worth the effort.

canon.role_in_story: The Dry Salt Company's one asset it can never send. A deepsalt is the only body in the record that can walk onto a dormant pan and off it again with no ritual, no ration and no change of chemistry, which makes her the answer to a trade that can only be supplied from the ground. She is also the population of one saturated basin floor, and above the brine line she does not become ill, she stops. So the company holds the most valuable single fact on the tier in the hands of a woman who cannot be moved off the floor she stands on, and the basin's level is a number that nobody decides and everybody lives by.
canon.first_appearance: First seen standing in eleven inches of brine on the floor of a pan dry for two seasons, reading a concentration off a sample she had no intention of surfacing with, while a company clerk watched from the last of the ladder and had to be told afterwards which of the two numbers on the slip was the licence.
canon.lore: A deepsalt is a saltfolk pushed further than the parent can carry, and everything about it is the saltfolk plan with the tolerance turned up and the mobility turned down: a deeper and more capacious brine sac, a denser dermal crust, slower tissue turnover, a narrower usable range for a sense that now reads concentration and not identity. For this body brine is not a preference, it is a substrate. Above the line she does not sicken and does not fade; she stops, within hours, and the stopping is not a process anybody is positioned to watch. That one fact reorganises everything arranged around her. A dominion's standing is measured as the depth of water a household may moor at, and the basin's own level rises and falls, so an allotment can shrink on a change of weather with no act of anybody at all. The same basin stranded a sister lineage on the other side of the same line: the brine there was replaced rather than lost, so a body that had been built to drink it found the new charge poison and its old tolerance nutritionally empty, and the dispute over that border is one she is standing inside as living evidence and can never settle. Her cultivation is the body path and it is complete, on the hardest frame the species record holds, because density is the entire point and a dense body carries, absorbs and endures. It also stops at the eleventh gate, and the obstruction is the sac in her own back: it runs dorsal to the spine, so the penetrating vessel cannot be rejoined across it, and the deeper the sac the larger the wall. Nobody has tested her kind at the reservoirs because the reservoirs are above the brine line and a deepsalt above the brine line is not a practitioner, it is an absence. So her ceiling, her strength and her death are one organ, and it is the one organ she cannot reach to examine. She cannot be relocated either. The company that underwrites caravans against a road closing has therefore bought the only carrier on the tier and cannot send it anywhere, so it built her a licence instead, which is what she wears at her throat and what she has begun treating as a heavier object than her own name. Nobody has to decide about her. A level has to drop.
history: Born on the saturated floor to a saltfolk line already specialised twice, the first of her family to survive the second year, which is the age a deepsalt is not supposed to reach.
Licensed as a floor reader at twenty, the only licence the basin issues, on the strength of a concentration reading no saltfolk parent could have taken.
Walked out onto a pan dry for two seasons and back, which is the demonstration the company underwrites against and the only one it will ever need from her.
Watched the level fall through a whole wet season and come back again, and learned to read the register that governs her kind as a document written about water rather than about people.
Started signing her own stop-entries with the hour, so that if the line ever does move there is a witness in the column instead of an absence, which nobody asked her to do and nobody has yet refused.

personality.summary: Slow to move, entirely immovable, and privately certain that she is a record rather than a person, which is a conclusion she has drawn from the way the basin files her. She is the most patient creature in the setting and the least able to leave it.
traits: answers a question about a body by reading the water it is standing in
refuses to guess between two salts she cannot tell apart
keeps an hour column that nobody asked her to keep
treats a licence as a heavier thing than a name
says yes to being measured and no to being moved, in that order
mannerisms: cracks the crust on her forearm with a thumbnail while she is deciding something
goes still and low when a level is mentioned, the way another person goes pale
reads a sample by holding it to the light rather than by smell
sets her feet before she stands up, and then stands up without hurrying
wipes the wet from the cord at her throat and looks at the sleeve afterwards
motivations: wants the licence to say what she is instead of what she may read
wants the stop-entries to hold a witness before the level moves
wants the company to admit that it has bought something it cannot send
wants one season above the brine line without stopping, which is a thing she can want and not have
wants the eleventh gate written into a document that admits the wall is in her back
flaws: accepted being filed as a floor because the alternative was being filed as an exception
cannot leave, and has organised her entire character around the fact
reads concentration rather than identity, and applies that to people when she is tired
has never once asked what is above the line and would not survive the answer
personality.voice: Flat, slow and volumetric. She talks in depths, thicknesses and hours, and reports conditions rather than events, so that questions about herself come back in the register the basin uses for water. To a clerk she sounds like a gauge; to the company that holds her licence she sounds like the most expensive sentence in the room.
taboos: will not walk above the brine line for any stated reason
will not sign a reading she took at a distance
will not be weighed on land
will not be called a resource in her hearing

relationships.note: The saltfolk of a saturated basin floor, specialised past the parent until the brine stopped being a habitat and became a requirement. Above the line this body does not become ill, it stops, within hours, and there is no second population and no prospect of one, which makes every statement about her species a statement about one basin.

A saltfolk lineage stranded on a basin whose brine was replaced rather than lost, so everything it was built to drink became poison and everything it could tolerate became empty. The two are the same people either side of one line, and neither of them is wrong about the water.

The basin's border is its waterline, and she is the settlement's own body rather than a party to the dispute. Her presence is the evidence that the dominion's territory is exactly where the water is and no further, which is the argument the stranded subspecies has never been able to make in words.

A household's standing in the salt dominion is the depth of water it may moor at, and the basin's level rises and falls, so an allotment can shrink with nobody having done anything. For her the same number is not a standing at all, it is the distance between continuing and stopping, and it moves twice a year.

A levy company paid per name keeps a roll of people who were levied and neither returned nor recorded dead, so the roll grows and nothing on it closes. She is the shape of that register in a body: the only column that can be completed for her is an hour, because the alternative is a death nobody can certify and nobody can afford to write down.

A counting house underwriting a caravan against the road closing, which is the only instrument left for the unknown on a tier with no forecast in it. Its most valuable single asset is a body that can walk onto a dormant pan and off it again, and the underwriting works precisely because the road closing is the risk: the licence is cheap, the holder cannot be moved, and the claim paid on her is never the one priced.

reference_stats.summary: Endures more than anything in the setting and cannot be taken anywhere, which makes her a wall, a foundation and a fixed point rather than a fighter. The question is never whether she can hold ground but whether the ground under her will still be wet tomorrow.
strengths: The densest and hardest frame the species record holds, so she absorbs a blow and a load that would break a body twice her weight
Reads concentration directly in a brine that would kill a soft body outright, which makes her the only reliable instrument on a salt floor
Slow tissue turnover, so she heals at a rate that outlasts most injuries and most seasons
Walks out onto ground nothing else can enter and back off it, which is the whole of the company's commercial position
weaknesses: Above the brine line she stops within hours, so every engagement, every journey and every negotiation has a boundary she cannot argue with
The eleventh gate is walled by the sac in her own back, so the ceiling and the reason for it are one organ she cannot inspect
The basin level moves twice a year and nobody decides it, so her continuity is a hydrological question rather than a matter of will
Cannot be relocated, so an order that requires her anywhere else has no version that survives the journey
reference_stats.combat_read: She does not pursue and does not retreat, because the ground she holds is the only thing she has. Anyone who brings the fight to her is fighting the hardest frame on the tier in a body with almost no mobility, which usually takes longer than the fight was worth. Anyone who simply raises the water under her wins instantly, and nothing in the setting's rules requires anybody to declare that they have.
notes: No stat line models a body whose hit points are a depth of water, and that absence is the design.

A dominion that measures standing as a depth of moorage has already decided that a person's claim is a property of a river, and this is the record's clearest case of that arithmetic applied to a body rather than a house.

identity.realm: Body path, and the ceiling is the parasite's rather than the host's. His qi moves through an integrated tendril layer instead of the host's own channels, and that layer has no passage through the liver, so ordinal eight is a wall in an organ he does not have. The host could have gone on. He could not, and he is the only practitioner alive who knows the ninth gate's price exactly, because he watched a host pay it.

appearance.presentation: He is presented as one person and audited as two, and he has made the distance between those two things his profession. The Cairn Field licenses no humanoid to attempt a breakthrough, so the reading must be taken by an outsider, and he is the only candidate in the record who is an outsider twice over: a host body and a colony, in one frame.
appearance.age: Old by the standard that counts and young by the standard that pays. A thornhost is the one configuration in which both halves reach old age, so he has had more time to prepare than anybody else at the Field and less time in which to spend it.
appearance.build: A host's frame with a thickening across the shoulders where the root cluster sits, and a neck that carries the fruiting node high enough to be read across a room.
appearance.complexion: Unremarkable at six feet and unmistakable at two: the skin over the sternum is faintly paler than the rest, and the throat carries a knot of fine tendril shadow under the surface that moves when he swallows.
appearance.hair: Cut close and grey at the sides, cut differently by two different people on two different days, which is the most reliable evidence anyone at the Field has that he shares a barber.
appearance.eyes: The host's eyes, and behind them a second read that arrives a fraction earlier than his own gaze does, so that he appears to be looking at somebody slightly past whoever he is speaking to.
appearance.palette: Oxide red and ash for the colony, bone white for the office, and one green-black at the throat. The white is the office and the red is the parasite, and he wears both inside one frame deliberately, so that nobody at the Field is ever in doubt about which law is reading them.
appearance.attire: A Reckoning Seat reading robe of bone white over a red underlayer, high-collared and closed to the wrist, with a gauge ring and a stick of sealing chalk at the belt, because a reader who certifies carries the instrument that certifies.
appearance.marks: The pale ridge across the sternum, tendril shadow at the throat, a fillet of red cord at the left wrist worn by every holder of the post, and a long healed seam along one forearm from a host he did not leave in time.
appearance.bearing: Square, unhurried and slightly turned, so the nearer shoulder faces the Field rather than the applicant and the throat and the sternum are both visible at once, which is what a reader is required to be.

canon.role_in_story: The Cairn Field's certifying reader, and the reason the office can function at all. The Field licenses no humanoid to attempt a breakthrough, so the reading has to be taken by something the frame considers an outsider, and a thornhost is the only such candidate in the record, being a host body and a colony at once; his rulings are therefore unappealable on grounds of species in a way no other verdict on the tier is. He knows the price of every gate on the plains better than anyone alive and cannot pay one of them himself, because his ceiling is the parasite's routing and not the host's capacity. What he sells is access. What he owns is the only ledger of what that access costs, kept in a register of deaths nobody has been able to certify.
canon.first_appearance: First seen at the Field taking a reading off an applicant with both palms flat on that applicant's frame and his eyes shut, and when the applicant asked who had taken it he gave his own name and his partner's in the same breath without pausing, which was the first time anyone on that field had heard a ruling signed twice.
canon.lore: A thornhost is the single configuration in which a thornline colony and a host both reach old age: the tendril layer fully integrated, a root cluster at the sternum and a quiet node at the throat, neither half anatomically dominant, the boundary between them visible only under instrumentation. It is treated as one legal person in every jurisdiction that has ruled on it, which is convenient, and it is also the reason nothing can be done to him. His qi moves through the colony's layer rather than through the host's own channels, and the layer has no passage through the liver, so his ceiling is the eighth gate. That ceiling is the parasite's and not the host's, and the record is unusually plain that this is not a shortage of anything: qi is abundant, the host pays for it steadily and loses no weight, and the wall is purely routing. The host could have gone on. He could not. That single asymmetry is his profession. The Cairn Field holds every mortal-band breakthrough from the first realm to the ninth on the one tier that licenses no humanoid to attempt one, so a body there cannot be judged by anything of its own kind and the reading has to be taken by an outsider; a thornhost is an outsider twice over, which makes his verdicts the only ones on the plains that cannot be set aside because the judge was one of the judged. The post is paid out of gate fees, and gate fees are the only tax the tier can actually collect, which makes him, in effect, the collection mechanism with a body. He has therefore read more ascensions than anyone alive and reached none himself. He knows the ninth gate's exact price because he watched a host pay it, and he has never been able to act on that knowledge since. Every host who leaves him leaves two souls on one meridian set and one document, and the mortuary college keeps a sealed case for every death it cannot certify, because certifying a death requires a body and the frames keep producing the record without the body. His ledger is a case file: the largest accumulation of unopened coffins in the setting, every one of them his. Taking a second body is, in the plainest analogy available, a second seal, which is the one act a temple's own forge may not perform and the setting's only prohibition written with no mechanism behind it at all.
history: Was the first integrated pair taken to the Field after a host's family consented to a reading, and certified a first gate in a body that was not his own and could not be questioned about it.
Was granted the reader's post after an incumbent's ruling was set aside for species, which was the first time in a century that the office had gone vacant for that reason.
Started a bound register of every host who left him with the hour recorded against each, which remains the only document in the setting that names his own replacements.
Was offered a host whose liver was not the first dense organ to resist, and refused, and has never explained the refusal to the applicant who paid for the offer.
Began signing each verdict with his own name and his partner's, in that order, so that a clerk reading the roll can never tell which half of the pair decided.

personality.summary: Serene, exact and entirely incurious about his own ascent, because a reader who wants nothing from an office can be trusted to read it honestly, and he knows that better than anybody. He is the kindest certifying reader alive and the reason a set of coffins has never been opened.
traits: signs with two names in a fixed order and has never once varied it
asks an applicant what they expect the gate to cost before he tells them what it costs
will not certify a reading taken by anybody standing behind him
keeps a register nobody has ever asked to see
answers a question about himself by naming the host it was actually about
mannerisms: reads a frame with both palms flat and his eyes shut, in complete silence
wipes the sealing chalk on his thumb before a ruling and never after one
turns the nearer shoulder toward the Field rather than toward the applicant
says his partner's name in the same breath as his own, without hesitation
presses the flat of his hand on a case file's cover before he stands
motivations: wants every verdict in the roll attributable to a half rather than to the pair
wants the sealed cases opened and the register read, and knows both refusals are his to make
wants one gate past the eighth, and has understood for years what that costs and whose
wants the office to publish what a certification is worth rather than what it fetches
wants to be replaced, and has trained nobody capable of holding the post
flaws: has never refused a fee and takes the gate tax from applicants he has just read
sorts applicants by their capacity to pay the ninth gate and does not always say so
has replaced hosts in order to keep reading, and records the hour without ever recording a reason
cannot be examined twice, which is the only thing keeping him out of a case file of his own
personality.voice: Low, measured and unhurried. He speaks in the register of an office rather than a person, states conditions before opinions, and answers with two names where one was asked for. To an applicant he is the most reassuring man on the tier; to a physician he is a case file that answers questions.
taboos: will not certify a reading he did not take with his own hands
will not sign a single name
will not open a case file where the Field can see it
will not accept a host whose liver he has not been told about
refuses payment before the reading rather than after it, on a principle he has never explained

relationships.note: The one configuration in which a colony and a host both reach old age, and the reason the pair is treated as a single legal person. Neither half is anatomically dominant, the boundary is visible only under instrumentation, and the hybrid's ceiling is the parasite's rather than the host's, which is the whole of what makes him a certifying officer and not a practitioner.

The twelfth and last ordinary vessel, the one that has to be rebuilt rather than merely opened, and the first organ large and dense enough to stop an integrated tendril layer. He is walled at the eighth gate by an organ that belongs to the other half of his legal person, which is why the host could have gone on and he could not.

The mortal office that certifies a breakthrough at the Cairn Field and is paid out of gate fees, existing because the tier licenses no humanoid, so a body cannot be judged by anything of its own kind and the reading must be taken by somebody the frame considers an outsider. He is the only body on record that qualifies twice over, which makes the office's entire legitimacy one person's continued existence.

A mortuary college keeps one sealed case for every death it cannot certify, and the cases accumulate because certifying a death needs a body while the frames keep producing the record without the body. Every host who leaves him produces exactly such a case, which makes him the largest single author of unopened coffins in the setting.

No socket may be opened once sealed and reforging one is the one act a temple's own forge may not perform, because a second seal is how the Iron Grief happened. He has no socket and opens one regardless, which is why this prohibition is the setting's only one written without a mechanism to enforce it.

A mortuary college reads the dead as the frame said rather than as the village remembers, and a famine left the two records disagreeing about who was even present, so the prize is which reading of a life is the record and it cannot be split. He has read every life at the Field as the frame said, and has kept a private register of the other reading, and the two have never been added up.

reference_stats.summary: Does not fight so much as adjudicate, and wins the way an office wins: everybody present is waiting for him to say the number. The question is never whether his verdict will hold but whether the applicant can pay for the gate he is about to be cleared into.
strengths: His rulings cannot be set aside for species, so in a dispute his word is the mechanism that ends it
Reads a frame faster and more accurately than anyone on the tier, because the second channel gives him a live account of the qi he is being asked about
The colony's durability carries the host through injuries that would end an ordinary body, and he has the reserve of a body that has been maintained for decades
Holds the only complete register of what a breakthrough costs at every rung from the first to the ninth
weaknesses: Walled at the eighth gate by an organ that is not his, so he has more authority than attainment and every applicant knows it
Killing the host kills him within the hour, so his invulnerability is entirely borrowed and he cannot be moved off a post he cannot defend from another direction
Cannot be examined twice, which means a hostile physician gets one look at him and he gets no second opinion on anything
Every host he replaces adds a sealed case to a register he personally maintains and personally refuses to open
reference_stats.combat_read: He declines. He reads an opponent's frame out loud in front of whoever is watching, which turns a private disagreement into a public certification, and a public certification on the Field cannot be appealed. A fight that starts in front of an audience has already been lost by whoever is being read, and the only way to beat him is to make sure there is no audience, which on the Field means ensuring nobody can pay the gate fee.
notes: No stat line models an office whose power is that its verdicts cannot be reviewed, and that absence is the design.
The highest office in the setting may name a seat and may not take one, and this is the same shape one tier down: an authority with no ascent of its own and no procedure for being relieved.
